name: FINUDA
notes: Kind hadron_structure is the nearest Atlas kind for strangeness nuclear physics; FINUDA is described as a fixed-target experiment at an e+e- collider (Franzini & Moulson 2006). It used kaons from φ decays, not e+e- collisions as such.
FINUDA and DEAR shared the second DAΦNE interaction point; KLOE sat at the first.

physics_goals.locator: FINUDA first-results paper (Phys. Lett. B 622, 2005), Introduction
physics_goals.quote: allows for the simultaneous measurement of observables like excitation energy spectra, lifetimes and partial decay widths for mesonic and non-mesonic decay, with high statistics and good energy resolution (better than 1 MeV)
physics_goals.value: Spectroscopy and decays of Λ-hypernuclei made by K⁻ stopped in thin targets: excitation spectra, lifetimes and mesonic and non-mesonic decay widths

summary.plain: A detector at Frascati's DAΦNE collider that stopped slow negative kaons from phi-meson decays in thin targets to make hypernuclei: nuclei in which a strange Λ particle replaces a nucleon. It took data in 2003-2004 and in 2006-2007.
summary.technical: FINUDA (FIsica NUcleare a DAΦNE): cylindrical magnetic spectrometer in a 1.0 T superconducting solenoid around DAΦNE's second interaction point, with eight thin nuclear targets, silicon microstrips, low-mass drift chambers, straw tubes and a scintillator time-of-flight barrel; K⁻ from φ → K⁺K⁻ stop in the targets (K⁻ stop + ᴬZ → ᴬΛZ + π⁻). Runs December 2003 to March 2004 and November 2006 to June 2007 (966 pb⁻¹ in the second); results include 12ΛC spectroscopy at 1.29 MeV FWHM and evidence for 6ΛH.

unique_capabilities.locator: FINUDA first-results paper (Phys. Lett. B 622, 2005), Section 2
unique_capabilities.quote: An important feature of the FINUDA apparatus (see fig. 2a) is the possibility to host eight different targets close to the interaction region
unique_capabilities.value: Eight thin nuclear targets next to the interaction region, so hypernuclei on different targets are measured in the same run
